title: Work order card at rest matches the design
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have an active staff member at the test location with the "Sales Representative" switch on: sales rep A.
  • Use a customer with no Sales Representative assigned.
  • Have a first work order for that customer, open and not invoiced, with nobody in Sales Representative.
  • Have a second work order with Sales Representative set to sales rep A.
  • Set the browser window to 1440 pixels wide with the zoom at 100%.
  • Open the design pictures "card-02-n1-rest.png" (board 1.2) and "card-05-n1-picked.png" (board 1.5) attached to this case beside the browser window at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Open the first work order in that browser window.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Without hovering, compare the Lead Technician, Service Advisor and Sales Representative rows with the picture of board 1.2.
  2. Open the second work order and compare the card with the picture of board 1.5.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • "Sales Representative" sits directly under Service Advisor.
  • Its label is on the first line and "Unassigned" on the second.
  • It has the same text style, size, weight and left edge as Lead Technician and Service Advisor.
  • There is no box, no arrow and no button at rest, as in the picture.
  • Measured on the screen, no blank strip remains under Lead Technician.
  • Every gap is 16 px, including the gap under Lead Technician.

Step 2:

  • The name, sales rep A, shows on the second line as plain text with no box, as in the picture.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11265 (Story 1, Give a work order its sales representative)

  • S1-R1: “The work order card shows a Sales Representative field directly under Service Advisor.”
  • S1-R2: “The field is the same field as Lead Technician and Service Advisor: the label "Sales Representative" sits inside it on the first line and the name on the second, in the same text style, size, weight and left edge.”
  • S1-R3: “At rest the field shows no box, no dropdown arrow and no buttons beside it.”
  • S1-R6: “The vertical gap between Lead Technician, Service Advisor and every Sales Representative field on the card is 16px. This holds with one field, with the Labor and Parts fields (S2-R5), and on the read-only card (S2-R17).”
  • S1-R6a: “A Lead Technician message shows directly below the Lead Technician field and pushes the fields under it down while it shows. With no message, the gaps are as in S1-R6.”
  • S1-R6a context note: “* Context note (S1-R6a): today the Lead Technician field on the card never shows a message: it isn't required and has no hint, so the 20px strip it used to keep was always empty. S1-R6a is the rule if a message is ever added. Test that no blank strip remains under Lead Technician and every gap is 16px.”
  • S1-R7: “With nobody assigned, the field reads "Unassigned".”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 40: “40. (b) Nothing triggers a message today. On the work order card, Lead Technician isn't required and has no hint, so it never shows one, and the 20px strip it kept was always empty. Please test that no blank strip remains under Lead Technician and that every gap is 16px. S1-R6a only applies if a message is added later. Context note added, PRD v11.”
